hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no signal, so a conv on edge 1->3 has nothing to pass on and gives little gain.
If node 1 is disconnected from the input, a conv on edge 1->2 only processes zeros, so its benefit is reduced.
With edge 2->3 removed, node 2 never reaches the output, so improving edge 0->2 cannot change accuracy.
Node 2's features are discarded when edge 5 is none, so a conv into node 2 has little effect.
When the direct input-to-output edge is already missing, removing edge 2->3 takes away one of only two remaining paths to the output, so accuracy drops more.
Without edge 0->3, the output depends more on edges 4 and 5, so deleting edge 4 hurts more.
If edge 2->3 is absent, removing edge 0->3 leaves only edge 1->3 feeding the output, which can collapse the network.
Replacing none adds a new path to the output, while replacing an existing op only swaps one operation for another, so the gain is larger.
Removing a 3x3 conv on edge 0 loses the most useful operation and cuts node 1 off, so it hurts more than removing a pool or skip.
Adding a residual skip where there was no edge improves gradient flow and trainability much more than replacing an existing op on edge 0->3.
